If you are self-employed, the business-use share of the loan interest is a deductible business expense (IRS Pub. 463). Employees can’t deduct it.

Section 179 (2026 tax year)

Business share of the cost–

Used more than 50% for business, a truck can qualify for Section 179 expensing of its business share. For SUVs and some trucks rated over 6,000 lb up to 14,000 lb gross vehicle weight the 2026 cap is $32,000, but a pickup with a cargo bed at least 6 feet long that you can’t reach from the cab isn’t subject to that cap. Trucks rated 6,000 lb or less follow the lower passenger-vehicle depreciation limits. Check the details with a tax professional.

At 50% business use or less, a vehicle doesn’t qualify for Section 179 expensing or bonus depreciation; the business share is depreciated on the slower straight-line schedule.

Personal-use trucks

For 2025 to 2028, interest on a loan taken out after 2024 for a new pickup with final assembly in the US and a gross vehicle weight rating under 14,000 lb may be deductible, up to $10,000 a year. The deduction shrinks once modified AGI passes $100,000 ($200,000 for joint filers). Used trucks and business use don’t qualify.
